corrections.before: Carrier-grade NAT. Your router does not have its own public IPv4 address, so inbound connections cannot reliably reach the host. Vast hosting requires a real public inbound TCP/UDP path; CGNAT and double NAT without public forwarding are not supported hosting setups. See [Network & Ports](/host/network-ports#cgnat-starlink-ipv6).
corrections.after: Carrier-grade NAT. Your router does not have its own public IPv4 address for inbound connections. Vast’s Host Setup guide requires public IPv4 and forwarded TCP/UDP ports for verification; CGNAT and double NAT without public forwarding do not provide that path. See [Network & Ports](/host/network-ports#cgnat-starlink-ipv6).

corrections.before: Externally reachable TCP/UDP ports forwarded to the host. Self-test requires at least 3 per listed GPU; production hosts should usually plan about 100 per listed GPU for headroom. See [Network & Ports](/host/network-ports#ports-per-gpu).
corrections.after: Externally reachable TCP/UDP ports forwarded to the host. The CLI self-test checks for at least 3 per listed GPU; the current Host Setup guide requires 5 and recommends 100 per GPU. See [Network & Ports](/host/network-ports#ports-per-gpu).

corrections.before: The renter workload running on your machine, usually a container or VM created from an offer.
corrections.after: A renter’s container or virtual machine created from an offer. An instance may be running or stopped.

corrections.before: Lower-priority bid rental. Higher bids run first; stopped containers and data remain on the machine. See [rental types](/guides/reference/faq/rental-types).
corrections.after: A lower-priority rental with a bid set by the renter. It can be stopped by a higher bid or an on-demand rental. See [rental types](/guides/reference/faq/rental-types).

corrections.before: Router behavior that makes same-LAN public-IP port tests unreliable. Test from outside the LAN. See [Network & Ports](/host/network-ports#test-ports-outside-lan).
corrections.after: Router support that lets devices behind the same NAT reach each other through their public address and ports. Without it, an internal public-IP test can fail; test external reachability from outside the LAN. See [Network & Ports](/host/network-ports#test-ports-outside-lan).

corrections.before: CLI diagnostic that checks requirements, rents a temporary instance, runs runtime tests, reports results, and cleans up. See [How to Self-Test](/host/how-to-self-test).
corrections.after: A CLI diagnostic that checks prerequisites and, when it can proceed, attempts a temporary rental, runtime tests, result reporting and cleanup. See [How to Self-Test](/host/how-to-self-test).

corrections.before: Passing self-test makes a machine eligible for verification. It does not guarantee verification, search placement, or rentals.
corrections.after: Passing self-test is one part of preparing for verification; the machine must also meet the published [verification requirements](/host/verification-stages#additional-requirements-for-verification). A pass does not guarantee verification, search placement or rentals.

corrections.before: The CLI first checks listing requirements. If preflight passes, it rents a temporary diagnostic instance, starts the self-test image, polls progress, reports results, and destroys the instance.
corrections.after: The CLI checks for a rentable offer and evaluates its reported requirements. If those checks allow the run, it attempts a temporary diagnostic rental, starts the selected image, polls progress and reports the result. It also attempts to destroy the temporary instance. If cleanup reports a failure, follow the displayed instructions to check and remove the remaining test instance.

corrections.before: Before renting the temporary diagnostic instance, the CLI checks whether the machine can be tested at all:
corrections.after: Before attempting the temporary diagnostic rental, the CLI looks for a rentable offer and checks its reported requirements:

corrections.before: - The API key can inspect the machine and offer.
corrections.after: - The API request can find a rentable offer. If no offer is found, diagnostics may query the machine and report access errors.

corrections.before: - GPU VRAM is greater than 7 GB per GPU.
corrections.after: - GPU VRAM is greater than 7 GiB per GPU.

corrections.before: - UDP echo on the mapped UDP port.
corrections.after: - UDP forwarding needs a separate check; the pinned CLI and self-test image do not perform a UDP echo test.

corrections.before: - GPU memory allocation, including ECC-capable memory allocation checks where applicable.
corrections.after: - GPU memory allocation targeting about 95% of each visible GPU’s VRAM. The stage is named “ECC” in the output, but it does not test ECC error correction.

corrections.before: If reliability is still `<= 0.90`, the installer may run with `--ignore-requirements` as a diagnostic. That does not qualify the machine for verification.
corrections.after: When the installer’s helper reaches its self-test command, it uses `--ignore-requirements` regardless of the current reliability value. Treat that result as diagnostic; it does not qualify the machine for verification.

corrections.before: Separate "listed" from "visible in a normal broad search." Marketplace search is not a complete inventory dump. It limits result sets, ranks and groups similar offers, tries to avoid race conditions, and usually shows the best matches first. Search can be affected by ranking, grouping, filters, verification state, offer state, rental state, reliability, price, supply and demand, or machine errors.
corrections.after: A listed machine need not appear in a broad search. Marketplace search returns a limited subset of offers and can group similar listings. Results depend on filters, offer and verification state, and ranking. Search directly by machine ID below before concluding that a machine is unlisted.

corrections.before: Vast is a GPU marketplace, not a managed setup service. Hosts operate their own hardware, OS, drivers, storage, networking, pricing, uptime, and maintenance.
corrections.after: Vast is a GPU marketplace. Hosts operate their own hardware, operating system, drivers, storage and networking, manage pricing, and plan uptime and maintenance.

corrections.before: - The host can run native Ubuntu/Linux.
corrections.after: - The host can run a supported Ubuntu Server release; see [Supported Hardware](/host/supported-hardware).

corrections.before: - The host can run native Ubuntu/Linux.
corrections.after: - The host can run a supported Ubuntu Server release; see [Supported Hardware](/host/supported-hardware).

corrections.before: | Mixed, old, or low-VRAM GPUs | Can fail checks or attract little demand. |
corrections.after: | Mixed, old, or low-VRAM GPUs | Check model and VRAM requirements before setup, and use Market Stats to assess current demand. |

corrections.before: Current listing guidance expects at least 128 GB of fast SSD storage per GPU. Docker storage should:
corrections.after: Current Setup guidance calls for SSD storage with at least a 200 GB dedicated partition for Docker. Plan additional capacity for the GPUs and workloads you intend to offer. Docker storage should:

corrections.before: - Mount predictably at boot before Docker and the host daemon start.
corrections.after: - Be mounted and ready before Docker and the host daemon start. If you use `nofail`, configure and verify the service dependencies separately; `nofail` alone does not ensure this ordering.

corrections.before: After editing `/etc/fstab`, mount and verify:
corrections.after: After editing `/etc/fstab`, mount any filesystem that is not already mounted and verify it below. `mount -a` does not apply new quota options to an existing mount. If project quota accounting is off, first arrange maintenance with no active rentals or storage users, stop the services using that filesystem, and perform a full unmount/mount or a planned reboot. Then check the resulting mount and quota state; a remount alone does not activate quota accounting.

corrections.before: The mount should be XFS, include `pquota` or `prjquota`, and show project quota accounting/enforcement as ON.
corrections.after: Verify that the mount is XFS, includes `pquota` or `prjquota`, and reports project quota accounting and enforcement as ON. If accounting is off, do not proceed with hosting: activate it through a full unmount/mount or planned reboot during maintenance, then repeat these checks.

corrections.before:
```bash
export VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE=/dev/mapper/vg1-lv--1
lsblk -f "$VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE"
findmnt -S "$VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE" || true
if findmnt -S "$VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE" >/dev/null; then
  sudo umount "$VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE"
fi
sudo mkfs.xfs -f "$VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE"
sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/docker
sudo blkid "$VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE"
```
corrections.after:
```bash
(
  VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE=/dev/mapper/vg1-lv--1  # Replace with your confirmed disposable device.
  [ -b "$VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE" ] || exit 1
  lsblk -f "$VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE" || exit 1
  findmnt -S "$VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE" || true
  printf 'Type the disposable device path to confirm formatting: '
  IFS= read -r VAST_FORMAT_CONFIRM || exit 1
  [ "$VAST_FORMAT_CONFIRM" = "$VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE" ] || exit 1
  if findmnt -S "$VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE" >/dev/null; then
    sudo umount "$VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE" || exit 1
  fi
  sudo mkfs.xfs -f "$VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE" &&
    sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/docker &&
    sudo blkid "$VAST_DOCKER_DEVICE"
)
```

corrections.before: Comment out any old `/data0` line for the same device, add the `/var/lib/docker` fstab line, then mount:
corrections.after: Replace the old `/data0` fstab entry for this same disposable device with a `/var/lib/docker` entry using its new filesystem UUID. Confirm that `/var/lib/docker` is not already mounted from another device before mounting and checking it below.

corrections.before: The mount should be XFS, include `pquota` or `prjquota`, and show project quota accounting/enforcement as ON.
corrections.after: Verify that the mount is XFS, includes `pquota` or `prjquota`, and reports project quota accounting and enforcement as ON. If accounting is off, do not proceed with hosting: activate it through a full unmount/mount or planned reboot during maintenance, then repeat these checks.

corrections.before: Move Docker's data root to a correctly mounted XFS filesystem, verify quotas, then restart Docker and the host software.
corrections.after: Plan the storage migration for maintenance with no active rentals or other storage users. Stop Docker and the host software, preserve the existing Docker data, move it to the intended XFS filesystem, and verify the mount and quotas before restarting the services. Do not format or replace a device that holds renter data.

corrections.before: The Host Installer Wizard should detect prepared Docker storage. If you use the [headless fallback installer](/host/installing-host-software#headless-fallback), pass the block device behind the Docker mount:
corrections.after: Review the prepared Docker storage in the Host Installer Wizard’s Storage step. If you use the [headless fallback installer](/host/installing-host-software#headless-fallback), use the installer downloaded from the official Setup page and pass the verified block device behind the Docker mount:

corrections.before:
```bash
sudo python3 ./install "$VAST_HOST_KEY" \
  --no-driver \
  --docker-partition /dev/mapper/vg1-lv--1 \
  --ports 40000 40799
```
corrections.after:
```bash
(
  # Replace the example device and port range with your prepared values.
  IFS= read -r -s -p "Paste current Vast host setup key: " VAST_HOST_KEY || exit 1
  printf '\n'
  [ -n "$VAST_HOST_KEY" ] || exit 1
  sudo python3 ./install "$VAST_HOST_KEY" \
    --no-driver \
    --docker-partition /dev/mapper/vg1-lv--1 \
    --ports 40000 40799
  VAST_INSTALL_RESULT=$?
  unset VAST_HOST_KEY
  exit "$VAST_INSTALL_RESULT"
)
```

corrections.before: | Software | Compatible NVIDIA/AMD driver stack, CUDA/runtime health, Docker/GPU runtime health, and a clean host. |
corrections.after: | Software | Compatible NVIDIA driver/CUDA stack, Docker/GPU runtime health, and a clean host. |

corrections.before: | DLPerf | Sustained real-world GPU throughput; PCIe, thermals, power, and drivers can affect it. |
corrections.after: | DLPerf | Estimated performance on typical deep-learning tasks; PCIe throughput, thermals, power, and drivers can affect measured performance. |

corrections.before: | Marketplace demand | In-demand GPUs, strong reliability, enough VRAM, and good network/location are more likely to be prioritized. |
corrections.after: | Marketplace demand | In-demand GPUs, strong reliability, enough VRAM, and good network are more likely to be prioritized. |

corrections.before: There is no fixed timeline. Passing self-test makes the machine eligible, but timing depends on automated checks, reliability, machine health, supply, demand, and platform policy.
corrections.after: There is no fixed timeline. Passing self-test is one part of preparation; verification also depends on the published requirements, automated checks, reliability, machine health, supply, demand and platform policy.

corrections.before:
```text
Unverified -> Verified -> Deverified -> Unverified
```
corrections.after:
```text
Unverified -> Verified
Verified -> Deverified (active machine error)
Deverified -> Verified (error cleared)
```

corrections.before:
Renters connect directly to the machine over the WAN, so it needs a public
IPv4 address with the port range forwarded to it. Machines behind CGNAT or a
shared ISP IP cannot be used for hosting.
corrections.after: Verification guidance requires a public IPv4 address with the port range forwarded to the machine. CGNAT and shared ISP IPs are not supported for this configuration.

corrections.before:
Use a separate SSH key pair for each machine you operate. One key reused across
your fleet means a single compromise exposes every machine you host.
corrections.after: Use a separate SSH key pair for each machine you operate. If a reused private key is compromised, every machine that trusts that key may be exposed; separate keys limit that shared access.

corrections.before:
You can check whether your machine is ready for verification by running a
Self-Test. See [How to Self-Test](/host/how-to-self-test).
corrections.after: Use Self-Test to check the CLI’s preflight requirements and run its diagnostic workload. Review the published verification requirements separately. See [How to Self-Test](/host/how-to-self-test).

corrections.before:
**Dedicated machines only.** Any personal workload, such as mining, gaming,
running your own jobs, or using the machine as a desktop, will automatically
fail verification.
corrections.after: **Keep the machine dedicated to Vast workloads.** Avoid local mining, gaming, desktop use or other jobs that compete with renter work. Run permitted jobs through the Jobs tab or `create job`. See [Workload Policy](/host/workload-policy).

corrections.before: - Network instability, closed ports, or low bandwidth.
corrections.after: - Network instability, closed ports or low bandwidth reported as an active machine error.

corrections.before: - GPU, NVML, Xid, PCIe, power, thermal, or storage errors.
corrections.after: - GPU, NVML, Xid, PCIe, power, thermal or storage problems reported as an active machine error.

corrections.before: Fix the underlying issue and wait for automation to refresh state. Most machine error states clear only after the platform sees sustained healthy behavior.
corrections.after: Fix the underlying issue and monitor the machine’s error and status. Some errors clear automatically after the platform detects recovery; others may need a Vast.ai team member to inspect and clear them. Clearing an error is distinct from manually selecting a machine for verification.

corrections.before: Single-GPU hosts usually have the lowest VM risk. Multi-GPU RTX 40-series hosts may also benefit. Multi-GPU datacenter hosts should be more cautious until VM P2P/NVLink behavior is a good fit for the workload.
corrections.after: Consider VM support for single-GPU machines and suitable multi-GPU RTX 40-series hosts after reviewing disk, network and workload needs. For multi-GPU datacenter hosts, the published VM guide recommends waiting for better VM P2P/NVLink support.

corrections.before: Apply and reboot:
corrections.after: During maintenance, after confirming there are no active rentals or other workloads, regenerate the GRUB configuration. Reboot only if that command succeeds:

corrections.before:
```bash
sudo update-grub
sudo reboot
```
corrections.after:
```bash
sudo update-grub && sudo reboot
```

corrections.before: Treat only exact `on` status, visible expected GPUs, and active Host services as a successful enablement. Treat `pending`, `off`, error or abort text, an unexpected status, a missing GPU, or an inactive service as a failure. If IOMMU groups are not set up, correct the BIOS and kernel IOMMU configuration, reboot, and verify the grouping before retrying.
corrections.after: Require exact `on` status, the expected GPUs and an `active` result for each listed service before proceeding. These are basic configuration and Host-health checks, not proof that a VM workload is healthy. Stop and investigate `pending`, `off`, error or abort text, an unexpected status, a missing GPU or an inactive service. If IOMMU groups are missing, correct the BIOS and kernel configuration, reboot during maintenance, and verify the grouping before retrying.

corrections.before: Set `--vol_size 0` when you do not want the machine listing to include a volume offer. Pass an explicit size and price so the advertised capacity is intentional.
corrections.after: Set `--vol_size 0` when you do not want the machine listing to include a volume offer. For a nonzero offer, pass an explicit size and price so the advertised capacity is intentional.

corrections.before:
You can publish GPU and volume offers together:

```bash
vastai list machine <machine-id> \
  --vol_size <capacity-gb> \
  --vol_price <usd-per-gb-month> \
  --end_date <date>
```

Set `--vol_size 0` when you do not want the machine listing to include a volume offer. Pass an explicit size and price so the advertised capacity is intentional.
corrections.after:
You can publish GPU and volume offers together:

```bash
vastai list machine <machine-id> \
  --vol_size <capacity-gb> \
  --vol_price <usd-per-gb-month> \
  --end_date <date>
```

Set `--vol_size 0` when you do not want the machine listing to include a volume offer. For a nonzero offer, pass an explicit size and price so the advertised capacity is intentional.
